clue.text: Garment that's a mistake when taking the Underground

parts.note: a boob is a silly blunder
the Tube is London's Underground railway

explanation.surface: Someone wears an unwise top for a ride on the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapless tight elastic top is a familiar item of women's clothing, so an example of a garment.

clue.text: Fast driver? Only 100 mph!

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
doing a ton is British slang for driving at a hundred miles an hour

explanation.surface: A sneer at a supposedly speedy motorist who manages a mere hundred miles an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenson Button is a British Formula One world champion, hence a fast driver; the question mark flags the proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: Names a speedy racing champion of Formula One, a definition by example of a quick motorist.

clue.text: Author died with nothing translated into French

parts.note: ob. abbreviates Latin obiit, he or she died
the French word for nothing is rien

explanation.surface: A writer passed away having left nothing rendered into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Flann and Edna, Irish novelists, share this surname, so it names a writer by example.

clue.text: Train's source of power is a controversial topic in LA

definitions.meaning: an electrified rail beside the running rails feeding current to trains
in American political idiom, an issue too dangerous to touch

explanation.surface: A transport writer notes how electric trains are fed, and that this is hotly disputed in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: The live conductor rail powers trains; in US slang, touching it means political death, hence an untouchable issue.

clue.text: Payment method taking account of former coins

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
ex- means former, as in ex-wife
change is loose coins

explanation.surface: A way of paying that accepts old money no longer in circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A written order to pay a sum on a given date is a traditional financial instrument for settling debts.

clue.text: Blue ice unfortunately contains decayed matter

indicators.note: the shuffled letters wrap around the next piece
suggests the letters of ice have come out badly arranged

parts.note: rot is decayed matter

explanation.surface: Sad ice that has gone off and holds rotten stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour to go with ice, but means smutty; 'unfortunately' gives EIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in British usage describes risque or smutty material, a synonym for sexually explicit.

clue.text: A doctor reset two bones

indicators.note: as a broken bone is reset, these letters are rearranged

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A doctor sets two broken bones back in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' turns A and DR into RAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm contains one of these on each side, so the plural names long bones in the arms.

clue.text: Gangsters in musical, turning up during a hit that's gone wrong

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits in the middle of the other
a hit gone wrong has its letters rearranged
in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Fame is a musical about a performing arts school

explanation.surface: Mobsters at a show botch a contract killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone wrong' gives THIA, split by the musical read upwards ('turning up').
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian-rooted organised crime syndicate is the archetypal gang of criminals.

clue.text: Meet with Italian church official briefly

parts.note: con is Italian for with

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a verger looks after a church interior

explanation.surface: Getting together with an Italian churchman for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people that come together at one point join up, a synonym for meeting.

clue.text: Deception used when producing recent EPs, perhaps

parts.note: rearranging the letters of pretences gives recent EPs, so these words are a counterfeit form of that word

explanation.surface: Trickery is used when producing new extended-play records.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'false' as an anagram signal on PRETENCES: its letters shuffled give RECENT EPS, so those words are a fake version of it; 'perhaps' marks this.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying about facts to gain advantage is the legal phrase for obtaining things by trickery.

clue.text: Famous couple from Ireland told van broke down

indicators.note: a vehicle breaking down signals these letters falling apart and reforming

explanation.surface: Someone from Ireland reports that their van has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: TORVILL AND DEAN are the British ice-dance pair who won Olympic gold in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: Jayne and Christopher, the celebrated skating duo, are a well-known pair, so this is an example.

clue.text: See 10
Upright, single, no date

parts.note: single means one
n.d. is the bibliographic abbreviation for no date

explanation.surface: An honest unmarried person without a partner for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing on its end describes something vertical, a phrase meaning erect.

clue.text: Stubborn stain to be specially treated

indicators.note: a stain specially treated is worked on, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A tough stain needs special treatment to shift it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig-headed person refuses to change their mind, a direct synonym for obdurate.

clue.text: Batman leaving Batmobile, perhaps for a service in Gotham City?

parts.note: a batman is an officer's personal servant in the British army, so a valet
leaving a car somewhere is parking it

explanation.surface: Batman abandons his famous car, perhaps for some job in his home city.
explanation.walkthrough: Batman is not the superhero here but a military servant; Gotham City is a jokey stand-in for New York, the question mark marking the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendants who take and leave your car at hotels or restaurants offer an American-style convenience.

clue.text: Drops measuring device?

parts.note: seems to say someone discards a measuring tool, but means an instrument for gauging falling drops of water

explanation.surface: Someone lets go of a measuring instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological instrument collects and records how much precipitation falls.

clue.text: Man sitting in vehicle changes colour of beards in paintings, we hear

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the chessman sits inside the next word

parts.note: dyes means changes the colour of
a man in chess, here the king, abbreviated K

explanation.surface: A man in a van changes the colour of the beards in some paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like Van Dyck's: the pointed beards are named after the painter Anthony van Dyck, whose portraits show them.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pointed chin beards are named after a Flemish portraitist whose sitters wore them.

clue.text: Large quantity of water in which girl, sick, has swallowed tablet

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the tablet
sick suggests the letters of has are disordered

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A poorly girl takes a pill in some body of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' turns HAS into HSA, which 'swallowed' wraps round E.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of sea between Britain and Ireland is a large body of water.

clue.text: Bit of paint needed, if renovating Carly's ice rink shortly

indicators.note: renovating means remaking, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order
rink is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Some paint is needed to do up Carly's skating venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic polymer forms the binder in many modern paints, so is one component of them.

clue.text: Home in castle in Hungarian capital

indicators.note: the word for home sits inside the castle

parts.note: a fort is a castle
in means at home

explanation.surface: A home inside a fortress in Budapest.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital means money here, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungary's currency unit is its money, so capital in the financial sense.

clue.text: Falling through ice as escapade finishes

indicators.note: in a down clue, the answer drops through the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A daring outing comes to an end when someone falls through the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Stops or comes to an end; the third-person verb matches the clue's finishes.

clue.text: Come out of joint as girl starts to strip languorously, taking off coat and first of earrings

parts.note: Di is short for Diana

indicators.note: takes the opening letters of the next two words
taking off is read as setting the letters of coat in motion, an anagram
takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A girl slowly undresses, removing her coat and an earring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone forced from its socket is displaced, so the verb means to be put out of joint.

clue.text: Postponed nothing pleasant

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Delayed, nothing was agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put in cold storage are held over for later, an idiom for deferred.

clue.text: Theatre-in-the-round

parts.note: the phrase for a stage with seating all around, here also meaning a playhouse that is itself a sphere

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Southwark playhouse bears the name of a sphere, so it is a round playhouse.

clue.text: Bussing money across the States for distant relatives

parts.note: to buss is an old word for to kiss

indicators.note: the coins stretch across, around, the abbreviation for America

parts.note: coins are money
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Transporting cash by bus across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bussing' looks like bus travel but means kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names relations distant enough to greet each other with a peck on the cheek, so remote kin.

clue.text: See 24
Fish girl brought on board

indicators.note: the girl is put within the ship's letters

parts.note: being on board means on a ship, SS being a steamship
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is taken aboard with the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray-like sea creature, the plural naming several of a kind of fish.

clue.text: Like an old footballer — great stuff, with a whiff of danger?

definitions.text: stuff, with a whiff of danger?

parts.note: as means like
George Best was a famous Manchester United and Northern Ireland footballer of the 1960s
OS is outsize, a clothing label for large

explanation.surface: Praise for a past footballer as brilliant, though slightly risky.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibrous mineral once used for insulation is a material dangerous if its dust is inhaled.
